patients.summary: Office administrative assistant with mild asthma, chronic hypertension on labetalol and a pack-a-day smoking habit, whose obstetric history (cervical insufficiency, an 18-week loss, a miscarriage, an ectopic, an abruption with postpartum hemorrhage) runs through her years with the practice. In December 2025 a high-speed collision at 22 weeks led to hemorrhagic shock, splenectomy and ARDS; she recovered and delivered at term in April 2026.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is a 27 y/o woman hoping to transfer her primary care to us. Previous office is closing its adult panel in December. She has asthma and high blood pressure and is on labetalol. Explained membership and that insurance is still billed for labs and specialists. She'd like the first open new-patient slot; booked 11/9 at 8:40. Release signed over the phone for records; request faxed to her former office today.

documents.title: Records received: prior primary care office
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Records received, 14 pages. Includes last two office notes, med list, immunization printout and a cervical cytology report from 03/2020 (negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy). Problem list on their end: asthma, hypertension, tobacco use. Meds: labetalol 200 mg BID, albuterol inhaler PRN, prenatal vitamin. NKDA. Filed for the provider to review before her 11/9 visit.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
27 y/o new to us. Prior office closing its panel. Records reviewed.

HTN: told she had high pressures early in her 2020 pregnancy; OB started labetalol 200 BID and she never came off it. Takes it most days, misses the evening dose now and then. No headaches, chest pain or swelling. Doesn't check at home.

Asthma: since her teens. Albuterol maybe twice a month, more with colds and smoke. No ED visits or oral steroids in years, no nighttime waking.

OB hx: cesarean 08/2020, one child at home. In September she lost a pregnancy at 18 weeks; she says the cervix opened without pain and the bag was bulging when she got to L&D, and she had a D&E. They told her it was cervical insufficiency. Still taking her prenatal vitamin. Tearful talking about it but says she's coping; partner and her mom are a help.

Tobacco: 1 ppd since about 18. Has tried cutting down, never a real quit attempt. Not interested in medication today, will think about it.
EtOH none. Works as an administrative assistant in an office.
FH: mother HTN. Maternal aunt had cervical insufficiency and a preterm baby. Paternal grandmother had asthma.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP above goal, see vitals. Well appearing. Lungs clear, no wheeze. RRR, no murmur. Abd soft. No edema.
PHQ-9 5.

A/P
1. Chronic HTN, above goal on labetalol. Adherence talk; keep 200 BID for now, recheck in a few months. CMP, lipids, UA today.
2. Mild intermittent asthma. Albuterol PRN, refills ok.
3. Nicotine dependence. Counseled. Revisit.
4. Hx cervical insufficiency / 18-wk loss. Recommended early OB contact with any future pregnancy given this history.
5. HM: Pap 03/2020 normal at prior office. HIV and HCV screen today. Flu shot today, L deltoid.
RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Your recent results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Yvette, your blood counts, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol, thyroid and urine all came back normal. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to change. Good to meet you on Tuesday.

BP check. Has been better about the evening labetalol since she set a phone alarm. Feels fine. Asthma quiet over the winter, one cold in January needed the inhaler for a week.
Still a pack a day. We talked about what quitting before another pregnancy would mean; she isn't ready, says work is stressful and it's how she gets through the afternoon.

BP improved today. Lungs clear.

A/P: HTN better controlled on labetalol 200 BID, continue. Asthma mild intermittent, stable. Smoking, counseled again, quitline number given. Follow up in 6 months or sooner if she becomes pregnant.

Still smoking, about a pack. Strongly encouraged cutting down; she'll try.

BP at goal. Abd soft, nontender.

documents.title: Emergency Department Note (outside)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of visit 06/27/2022.
28F G3P1 at about 7 weeks by LMP, + home test 3 weeks ago, with 6 hours of severe lower abdominal cramping and heavy bleeding, through several pads. Hx chronic HTN on labetalol, asthma, prior 18-week loss attributed to cervical insufficiency, prior cesarean. NKDA. Smoker.
Arrival BP 100/60, HR 110, T 37.2. Suprapubic tenderness, no rebound or guarding. Speculum: os open, moderate blood, no tissue in canal or vault.
Hgb 10.2. Quant hCG 50 (1500 one week ago per patient's PCP draw). A positive, no RhIG indicated.
TVUS: empty uterus, no IUP, no ectopic.
Impression: complete spontaneous abortion, first trimester. Hemodynamics improved with IV fluids. Discharged with bleeding precautions, f/u PCP and OB in 1 week. Scanned to chart.

documents.title: Call after ED visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called her after seeing the ED note. Bleeding down to a light period now, cramps easing with Tylenol. No fever, not dizzy. Very sad, partner home with her this week. Work note given for the rest of the week. OB intake was not yet scheduled, so referral closed for now. Office visit next week with a blood count.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after ED visit 6/27 for a complete first-trimester miscarriage. Bleeding stopped 7/2. No fever, no pelvic pain now. Back at work Monday.
Mood low but functioning, sleeping ok. PHQ-9 6. Declines counseling referral for now; knows how to reach us.
Wants to try again. Discussed that an early loss like this is a different thing from what happened at 18 weeks, and that her OB should see her early next time.

BP fine. Abd soft, nontender.

A/P: Complete SAB, resolved clinically. CBC today. Continue labetalol, prenatal vitamin. Physical in September.

documents.title: CBC
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 11.8, up from 10.2 in the ED. No iron needed. Portal message sent.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
28F for physical. Feeling more like herself since the summer. LMP mid-August; she and her partner are trying again.
HTN on labetalol 200 BID, no side effects. Asthma: inhaler a few times a month. Smoking 1 ppd, cut down for a week in July then back up.
No alcohol. Works full time, little one in daycare.
ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: well. HEENT normal. Thyroid not enlarged. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. Abd soft. Skin no rashes. No edema.
PHQ-9 3.

A/P
- HTN controlled. Continue.
- Asthma, mild intermittent. Continue albuterol PRN.
- Tobacco: counseled; she wants to quit 'once things settle.'
- Preconception: on prenatal vitamin. Early OB contact if positive.
- HM: Pap due 2023. Flu shot next month. Fasting labs drawn today.

documents.title: Physical labs

documents.body: CBC, CMP, lipids and UA all normal. Hemoglobin back to her baseline. Portal note sent.

medications.sig: Insert 1 capsule vaginally at bedtime until 36 weeks

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
22 weeks today by LMP 8/10. Being followed by the high-risk OB group. Saw them 12/28 for her 20-week visit: she says the cervix was closed, and the ultrasound measured it at 25 mm with no funneling. They told her that's on the short side given her history, called it cervical insufficiency, and started vaginal progesterone 200 mg nightly to continue until 36 weeks. No letter from them yet; requested.
No bleeding, discharge, cramping or leakage. Feeling movement. Worried about a repeat of last year but trying to stay positive.
Labetalol 200 BID, taking reliably. Asthma quiet. Smoking about half a pack; she's trying.

BP at goal. Lungs clear. Gravid abdomen, nontender.

A/P
1. Chronic HTN in pregnancy, controlled on labetalol. OB co-managing.
2. Cervical insufficiency, on progesterone per OB. Added to list.
3. Tobacco: congratulated on cutting back, encouraged to keep going.
4. Asthma stable.
See her after delivery unless something comes up.

documents.title: Discharge Summary (outside)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Regional hospital, antepartum unit. Admitted 02/25/2023 via ED, discharged 02/28/2023.
28 y/o G4P1 at 28w3d presented with a day of fever, chills, R flank pain and nausea, after several days of dysuria and urgency she assumed were from pregnancy. Pain started in the low back and moved up toward the flank. Bacteriuria screen sent in the first trimester was never followed up.
On arrival T 38.7, HR 112, BP 106/66. Looked unwell. R CVA tenderness, abdomen without rebound or guarding.
UA nitrite positive with pyuria and bacteriuria. Renal US: mild R hydronephrosis.
NST reactive.
Dx: acute pyelonephritis in pregnancy.
Course: IV ceftriaxone, afebrile within 36 hours, tolerating PO. Fetal status reassuring throughout.
Discharge meds: cephalexin 500 mg QID to complete 14 days total; continue labetalol 200 mg BID, vaginal progesterone nightly, prenatal vitamin.
Follow up with OB in 1 week and with PCP.

conditions.label: Acute pyelonephritis in pregnancy, third trimester

Hospital 2/25-2/28 for right pyelonephritis at 28 weeks, discharge summary reviewed. Finishing cephalexin, two days left. No fever since discharge, flank pain gone, urinating normally. Baby moving well; saw OB Friday.
Still on labetalol and nightly progesterone.

Afebrile. BP fine. No CVA tenderness. Lungs clear.

A/P: Pyelonephritis in pregnancy, clinically resolved on antibiotics. Finish course. Told her to call the same day for burning, fever or flank pain, and that OB will likely recheck her urine. HTN controlled.

conditions.label: Ruptured left tubal ectopic pregnancy with hemodynamic instability

reports.text: Transvaginal technique. No intrauterine gestational sac. Complex mass in the left adnexa separate from the ovary. Free fluid in the pelvis. Right adnexa unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Empty uterus with complex left adnexal mass and pelvic free fluid, consistent with ruptured left ectopic pregnancy in this clinical setting.

documents.title: ED and Operative Note (outside)
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Regional hospital. Visit 12/23/2023, discharged 12/24.
29F, LMP about 6 weeks ago with a history of irregular cycles, woke with sudden severe lower abdominal pain, 6 hours before arrival. One partner, no contraception. History: chronic HTN on labetalol, asthma, cervical insufficiency with prior 18-week loss, cesarean 2020, vaginal delivery 05/2023.
BP 90/60, HR 120, T 37.2. Pale and anxious. Diffuse tenderness with rebound and guarding; cervical motion tenderness.
Hgb 9.2. hCG 3500.
TVUS: no IUP, complex L adnexal mass, pelvic free fluid.
Taken to the OR emergently: laparoscopy showed a ruptured left tubal ectopic with hemoperitoneum, left salpingectomy performed. Right tube normal in appearance.
Recovered well, discharged POD1 tolerating diet. A positive, no RhIG.
F/u gyn 2 weeks, PCP for blood count.

conditions.label: Ruptured left tubal ectopic pregnancy with hemodynamic instability

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Twelve days after laparoscopic left salpingectomy for a ruptured ectopic (outside note reviewed). Incisions healing, mild soreness at the umbilical site, off pain medicine. Light spotting stopped. Tired but eating fine, walking.
Shaken by it, says her partner is too. They are not sure about more pregnancies; I pointed out the right tube was normal and that the gyn team is the best place for that conversation.
Labetalol continued through the admission.

BP at goal. HR normal. Three small laparoscopic incisions healing well. Abd soft, mildly tender at the umbilicus only.

A/P: S/p left salpingectomy for ruptured ectopic, recovering. CBC today. Gyn f/u next week as planned.

events.reason: abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding at term

conditions.label: Postpartum hemorrhage
conditions.note: uterine atony after vacuum-assisted vaginal delivery

documents.title: Discharge Summary (outside)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Regional hospital labor and delivery. Admitted 12/31/2024, discharged 01/03/2025.
30 y/o at 38w0d with chronic HTN on labetalol, asthma, cervical insufficiency with prior 18-week loss, prior cesarean x1, prior vaginal birth, L salpingectomy for ectopic, presented with an hour of sudden severe abdominal pain and dark vaginal bleeding. No trauma or fall.
BP 155/100, HR 98, T 37.2. Abdomen tense and tender, uterus firm and irritable. FHT 140. Speculum: moderate dark red blood, cervix closed, no placental tissue seen. Hgb 9.8 on arrival; coags within normal limits.
Assessment: placental abruption. Fetal tracing reassuring; she went into labor that morning and labored with close monitoring. Prolonged second stage, vacuum-assisted vaginal delivery of a healthy boy. Placenta delivered intact.
Shortly after, brisk bleeding with a boggy enlarged uterus; BP 90/60, HR 110, pale and anxious. Bimanual massage, second IV line, uterotonics; bleeding controlled. Postpartum hemorrhage with acute blood loss anemia.
Remainder of stay uncomplicated. Pressures managed on home labetalol.
Discharge meds: labetalol 200 mg BID, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, prenatal vitamin, albuterol PRN.
Follow up: PCP within 2 weeks for blood count; OB 6 weeks.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Discharge summary from L&D received today. Called pt: home since Friday with the baby boy. Bleeding like a heavy period and slowing. Lightheaded getting up fast the first two days, better now. Taking labetalol, iron and prenatal. No headache, vision changes or chest pain. Booked with PCP 1/14 for CBC and BP. Told her to call or go to the ED for soaking a pad an hour, fainting or fever.

events.reason: follow-up after delivery and postpartum hemorrhage

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two weeks after delivery. Admitted 12/31 with a placental abruption at 38 weeks, vacuum-assisted vaginal birth of a healthy boy, then a postpartum hemorrhage from atony treated with massage and uterotonics. Summary reviewed.
Now: lochia light. Fatigue, mild lightheadedness on stairs, improving. No chest pain, palpitations or dyspnea. Taking ferrous sulfate daily, tolerating it. Labetalol 200 BID. Bottle feeding.
Sleep broken, mood up and down but enjoying the baby. PHQ-9 6. Partner off work for two weeks.
Smoking: back to a pack.

BP ok. HR normal. Pale conjunctivae. Lungs clear. Fundus firm, below umbilicus. No calf tenderness.

A/P
1. Acute posthemorrhagic anemia: Hgb pending today. Continue iron 325 daily, recheck in about 3 months.
2. PPH, resolved.
3. Chronic HTN, controlled on labetalol.
4. Mood: watch closely; she'll message if worse. Rescreen at next visit.
5. Tobacco: counseled.

documents.title: CBC
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 9.4. Heading the right direction for two weeks out. Continue iron.

events.reason: severe abdominal pain and dizziness after high-speed motor vehicle collision

results.test: Carbon dioxide partial pressure in Arterial blood
Oxygen partial pressure in Arterial blood

reports.text: Focused assessment with sonography for trauma, bedside. Free fluid in the abdomen. Gravid uterus.
Portable AP. Endotracheal tube in place. Bilateral alveolar infiltrates. No pneumothorax.

documents.title: Discharge Summary (outside)
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
Regional trauma center. Admitted 12/28/2025, discharged 01/20/2026.
31 y/o G7 at 22w0d, uncomplicated pregnancy to date, restrained driver in a high-speed collision with airbag deployment. Arrived awake with severe abdominal pain and dizziness. PMH chronic HTN on labetalol, asthma, cervical insufficiency, prior abruption with PPH, prior ectopic s/p L salpingectomy, prior cesarean. NKDA. Smoker 1 ppd x 10 yrs.
BP 85/50, HR 120, RR 22, dropping to 75/45 despite crystalloid. Cool and clammy. Diffuse abdominal tenderness, uterine contractions, small amount of vaginal bleeding. FHT 140.
Hgb 9.0, PT 14. FAST positive for free abdominal fluid.
Hemorrhagic shock with acute coagulopathy: massive transfusion protocol. Became increasingly short of breath and confused, intubated in the ED. Exploratory laparotomy: splenic laceration with hemoperitoneum, splenectomy. Uterus not entered.
To ICU about 4 hours after the collision: BP 95/60, HR 122, RR 28 on the vent, SpO2 88% on FiO2 1.0. Diffuse bilateral crackles. ABG on 100%: pH 7.32, PaCO2 48, PaO2 58, HCO3 24. Lactate 3.2. CXR bilateral alveolar infiltrates.
ARDS with refractory hypoxemia: lung-protective ventilation, prone positioning. Oxygenation improved over the following week; extubated 01/07. Contractions settled early; OB followed daily, fetal checks reassuring throughout.
Discharged home 01/20 on room air.
Discharge meds: labetalol 200 mg BID, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, acetaminophen 500 mg 1-2 tabs q6h PRN, prenatal vitamin, albuterol PRN.
Needs post-splenectomy vaccines through PCP. Follow up: PCP 1 week, OB 1 week, trauma clinic 2 weeks, pulmonary 6-8 weeks.

reports.text: Good effort, acceptable and reproducible. FEV1, FVC and FEV1/FVC within normal limits. No obstruction or restriction pattern.
PA and lateral with abdominal shielding. Lungs clear. No effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal.
reports.conclusion: No acute cardiopulmonary findings. Prior infiltrates have cleared.

documents.title: Pulmonary Consultation (outside)
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outpatient pulmonary clinic, visit 03/10/2026. Thank you for the referral.
31F, now about 32 weeks pregnant, seen ten weeks after ARDS following trauma with hemorrhagic shock (ventilated, proned, extubated 01/07). Background mild intermittent asthma on albuterol PRN; current smoker.
She reports no dyspnea at her usual activity now, climbs stairs without stopping. No cough or wheeze.
Resting SpO2 normal on room air. Lungs clear throughout. No clubbing.
Spirometry normal. Chest radiograph clear; the infiltrates have resolved.
Impression: recovered from ARDS with normal lung function. No further pulmonary follow-up needed. Smoking cessation strongly advised. Return as needed.
